notes: forces_iff : Forces N <-> 3150 <= N; upper bound by kernel-checked LRAT (OpenProblemsLib.LRAT, 126702 RUP steps in 375 chunk theorems, about 62 min; LRAT data 24 MB not in git, see NT/E29.1/lrat/README.md), lower bound by the explicit colouring. Outside Lean: none. The statement rests on reading Guy's question as Forces (x < y, interval starting at 3).
summary_override: Least N = 3150, proved in Lean (forces_iff). Lower bound: explicit colouring of [3,3149]. Upper bound: [3,3150] CNF, defined in Lean from the problem, is UNSAT by a kernel-checked LRAT certificate (CaDiCaL 2.1.3, 126 702 RUP steps). No published [3,N] value found (Bowen arXiv 2205.12921 and follow-ups cite only Graham 252 and Hindman 990).

notes: Outside Lean: that the 9800-clause CNF (certificate/e44.cnf, from e44_sat.py) encodes the geometry: signotope encoding of x-sorted points in general position and the exact 'segment meets open triangle' test. The CNF's unsatisfiability is kernel-checked (birch_cnf_unsat, OpenProblemsLib.LRAT, 20 s). False for degenerate sets (7 collinear + 1).
